name: Australian Patience
description: Australian Patience is a strategic solitaire game that blends the layout of Klondike with the move-logic of Scorpion. It is characterized by having all tableau cards face-up from the start, requiring the player to build down in suit. Unlike Klondike, any cards sitting on top of a card being moved are carried along, making it a game of foresight and column management.

content.text: Australian Patience is a strategic solitaire game that blends the layout of Klondike with the move-logic of Scorpion. It is characterized by having all tableau cards face-up from the start, requiring the player to build down in suit. Unlike Klondike, any cards sitting on top of a card being moved are carried along, making it a game of foresight and column management.
Originating in Australia as a more skill-based alternative to Klondike. It gained international popularity in the digital era as part of high-difficulty solitaire collections.

One player for the standard solitaire game. The player shuffles and deals their own tableau; there is no dealer or opponent. Australian Patience can also be played competitively by two players (each with their own 52-card pack and tableau), but the primary form documented here is single-player.
7 columns of 4 cards are dealt face-up, slightly overlapped. This uses 28 cards. The remaining 24 cards form the draw pile (stock).

items.text: Competitive Australian: Two players play with their own decks. The first to clear their foundations wins.
